structure: Part 11 mined all 21 traces of identification.fit.spec.js's two validation describes: 'animal identification identifier validation' (7 tests: the empty-record test at line 619, the five 58-character identifier tests at line 636 for Microchip, Tattoo, Passport, Ear tag and Horse name, and the microchip error-state axe test at line 653) and 'animal identification address validation' (14 tests: six empty-mandatory-field tests at line 681 and eight over-length tests at line 700). The spec file was read in full for test titles and assertions. The traces were written by a newer Playwright than tim's trace viewer supports (tim distil trace open fails with TraceVersionError), so each zip's already-unpacked contents in the part11 working folder were read with jq: the test.trace action list, the page's final frame snapshot holding the error summary, and the network log's POST to the identification page. Every trace walks the same set-up (stub sign-in, start a notification, country of origin, 'What are you importing?', species, animal count on consignment details, then the overview's 'Identification details' link) to one page, /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/commodities/identification, headed 'Identification details', which re-renders with an error summary after a POST. Three commodity cards appear across the traces: Cat (01061900) — Felis catus (microchip, passport, tattoo, plus the permanent address block of eight fields), Cow (0102) — Bos taurus (ear tag, passport, no address block) and Horse (0101) — Equus caballus (microchip, passport, horse name, no address block). Conditional surface: the in-card 'Save and add another' button appears only when the line's count is above one (count 2 cat traces) and is absent on count-1 lines; the address block appears only on the cat card. Every error page showed exactly one error. All 21 tests passed; the axe test recorded no serious or critical violations. No network call other than the page's own GET and POST is visible in the browser's log.

claims.statement: No trace drives a format check on the email address, phone number or postcode (only empty and over-length values), so whether an invalid format is rejected, and with what message, is not shown.

No trace drives the mandatory-address errors through 'Save and continue' or 'Save and return to overview', nor the identifier length errors through 'Save and add another', so whether each rule fires on every save path is not shown.
No trace shows the validation of a second or later card (index 1 and on) or of a dog or ferret card, so error linking beyond the first card is not shown.
